review: M3-J1 r1 law and method soundness

requiredFindings.problem: The first-applicable precedence rule selects the committed-latched F39 projection from state 3 alone, before considering CommitUndetermined. State 3 does not prove a committed Run.
evidence: Item 8.3 rule 1 at :410 selects X7's F39 row and runId for state 3; rule 2 at :411 handles uncertainty only afterward.
X3D:170 preserves an undetermined evidence COMMIT even after a latch; X7:100-101 distinguishes Committed with a latch from CommitUndetermined with an ExecutionId and no RunId.
Pinned product commit_session.rs:943-983 can return CommitUndetermined after FinalGate admission and a latch, without constructing PublishedCommit.
Phase C at :405, matrix row 38 at :521 and S12-U at :570 require the durability row in that case.
requiredFindings.fix: Put CommitUndetermined first, or require the actual Committed(PublishedCommit) outcome in rule 1. Determine the outcome before applying the sampled latch. Make J-C14 and S12-U verify this precedence.

requiredFindings.problem: The proposed settlement point precedes required rendering, so it does not satisfy the governing definition of every required step being terminal. S12-D then injects at a point after this boundary but expects phase D.
evidence: The required render step is declared at :261; :421 puts the decision point before SOP2 finalization and before rendering, and :287 declares settlement there.
WS:224-228 and OPP:337-338 distinguish before/after settlement by actual required-step terminality. X7:85 and pinned finalization.rs:310-318 include rendering and output in required delivery.
SOP2:623 finalizes after the result is decided and before envelope rendering; it does not prove completed rendering.
S12-D at :571 holds x7.delivery.required.before. Pinned finalization.rs:283-318 reaches that point in delivery before invoking the renderer; J1 orders delivery after its decision point.

A required render failure can still change the outcome after the proposed settlement point, despite phase E saying the decided class stands. bootstrap.rs:57-58 independently forbids a replacement envelope after output begins.
requiredFindings.fix: Separate actual step terminality from the output decision/emission boundary. If final-envelope emission needs cancellation deferral, explicitly reconcile and successor-gate that exception with WS/OPP rather than declaring unperformed rendering terminal. Move the phase-D control to a genuinely cancellable point and add a post-decision control. Preserve single-envelope delivery.

requiredFindings.problem: Creation disclosure exists only in the successful DurableEntry, so Published followed by an attempt-B admission failure loses firstUse and backup-status information on the error path.
evidence: The entry at :149 returns Result<DurableEntry, InstallationTermination>; :166 places created metadata only in DurableEntry.
After Published, :164 runs fresh ordinary producers, gate and rechecks, any of which can fail before R3 succeeds.
Item 9 at :467 starts durable retentionDisclosure only after R3 succeeds, while :172 promises firstUse:true on later refusals after Published.

Pinned installation_routing.rs:107-118 already has the corresponding information-loss shape: entered is known, gate failures return only the termination, and entered reaches the caller only on success.
ENV7:790 excludes retentionDisclosure from the empty-errors interrupted branch, but ordinary gate/budget/barrier failure envelopes do not have that exclusion.
requiredFindings.fix: Carry value-only creation metadata on entry failures as well as success, sourced from the actual Published result and conveying no attempt-A authority. Start non-interrupted creation disclosure at publication rather than successful R3. Add Published-to-attempt-B producer, gate and barrier failure controls; retain false firstUse for LostRace/NotPristine and notice-only disclosure for the restricted interrupted branch.

requiredFindings.problem: The law specifies ExecutionId draws but no uniqueness-checked operational reservation before their use, particularly provider use before durable attempt custody.
evidence: IE:77-81 requires pre-use uniqueness reservation for both identities in every mode; :83-88 makes durable attempt custody a separate additional requirement.
J1 supplies process reservation for RequestId at :121-124 but only draws for the creation, durable, ephemeral and render ExecutionIds at :126-130.
Providers use the durable ExecutionId at J-ζ before prepare_commit inserts the attempt row.
Pinned CommitSession::open at commit_session.rs:327-372 draws and stores the identity without identity-registry reservation; request.rs:18-40 reserves RequestIds only.
One invocation has multiple ExecutionId draws, so the one-request-per-process restriction does not eliminate within-process identity reuse.
requiredFindings.fix: Specify and gate the process-custody reservation owner for every ExecutionId before P0, provider frames or operational records use it. Keep it distinct from later attempt_custody and preserve the security-owned durable draw. Update the identity/session successors and affected units, with a collision control that emits no unreserved or caller-selected identity. No permanent identity ledger is required.

requiredFindings.problem: J3d's durable end-to-end dependency list drops F2 and G3, which both the accepted plan and exact draft-r5 context pin require for J3.
evidence: Accepted M3-PLAN-r4.md:218 requires J2, F2 and G3 for J3.
The requested M3-PLAN.md draft-r5 pin repeats F2 and G3 at :211 and :303.
J3d at :611 has J2b, J3a, J3b, X3c-3, S13 and S16; neither F2 nor G3 appears.
J2b's enumerated J2 set at :607 does not inherit F2 or G3, and J3a/J3b are security/finalization units.
requiredFindings.fix: Add F2 and G3 to J3d or an explicit inherited predecessor. Preserve these gates in the conditional critical-path statement alongside J3a/J3b, X3c-3 and serialized lead-set completion. Assumed early finishes do not remove dependencies.

requiredFindings.problem: The claimed total outcome matrix lacks reachable native-context, Cargo-adapter and authenticated-release admission refusal families with distinct governing routes.
evidence: NE:3530 routes native-context closure/tool/compiler and universe-binding refusals to request-rejected / REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED before PlanId.
NE:3531-3532 routes native.prepare-bound-exceeded and native.ambient-cargo-config to operational-failed / HOST.IO_FAILURE; pinned M3-C r4:640 expressly requires the ambient Cargo control.
NE:3540 and :3574 separately route invalid authenticated release declarations to request-rejected / REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED.
The listed conditions are not missing-provider indeterminate (row 27), a just-built Plan invariant (29), worker faults (30/32), capability REQUEST errors (26), or capture/discovery I/O (23).
The law requires one control per reachable matrix row and treats an unmapped detail as a model error. Naming NE's full tables in J2a does not complete the matrix's conditions.
requiredFindings.fix: Add these families or explicitly broaden the appropriate rows with the exact NE class, code, fault cause, origin and detail-carrier rules. Keep unregistered internal keys in operational records. Add context/release and Cargo-adapter controls without new public codes.

requiredFindings.problem: The future M4 CLI instruction replaces audit's refusal before its comparison/module prerequisite, which is M5.
evidence: Item 1 at :85 explicitly places audit/comparison at M5, but :88 requires the M4 CLI unit to replace all four refusals at once.
BP:955 assigns audit to M5; BP:895 forbids command delivery before its module prerequisite.
X11:28 is an earlier prospective all-four replacement sentence whose M3 timing J1 already revises; it cannot override BP's command schedule.
requiredFindings.fix: Retain every M3 binary refusal and reconcile X11's prospective sentence with command milestones: default/analyze/fit at M4 after full prerequisites, audit at M5. Alternatively defer collective replacement to the latest prerequisite and stop calling it M4 enablement.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: A consuming method enforces one use of a token, but cancellation_latch(&self) can mint multiple tokens unless mint-once ownership is separately specified. Window closure also needs one synchronization order with a racing latch and coverage of refused/uncertain returns.
evidence: The proposed getter takes &self and returns a CancellationLatch; no unique take or mint-once failure is specified.
The window closes at publish's sample, while the pinned product samples the latch in the successful branch and returns uncertainty separately.
The law requires outside-window calls to change nothing and J-C15 requires a second latch to fail compilation.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestion: Specify whether single-use is per token or operation, enforce unique ownership when intended, and require synchronized sample/window closure on every outcome in S10/J3b's evidence.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The pipeline calls SOP2 finalization, but item 14 does not name O1 or a reviewed predecessor that supplies its callable implementation.
evidence: J-κ and the revised X7 order call SOP2's finalizer.
The plan assigns the S-OP-2 nonpersistent sink/finalization implementation to O1.
J3d's dependency list omits O1; SOP2's pinned r4 is still in review.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestion: Name the O1 dependency or the reviewed callable boundary available before it integrates; optional observability loss does not itself define an absent API.

requestedDecisions.x11Successor: M3 library-only scope and continued binary refusals are sound. Future audit enablement needs J1-R7; identity and first-use termination obligations need J1-R3/R4.
requestedDecisions.firstUse: The charged non-authoritative probe, original-owner rechecks, fresh token-gated attempt B and one-gate rule are sound. Present-to-Absent uses the existing NOT_INITIALIZED row. Error-path creation metadata needs J1-R3.
requestedDecisions.firstUseOrderAndStorageChoice: R0-R12 preserves pinned X12 r4 and M3-B/M3-C ordering; pure S3.1 before project effects is sound. X12 acceptance is not granted here.
requestedDecisions.sessionAtHandoff: Opening at R12 uses the existing draw/getter, gives providers the same identity as the receipt and adds no durability point by itself. Pre-use reservation still needs J1-R4.
requestedDecisions.cancellation: The existing two-bit gate and operator REV preserve the basic stop/settlement rules. Outcome precedence and settlement/control placement require J1-R1/R2; token/window implementation precision is J1-N1.
requestedDecisions.backupStatus: Published-only firstUse, exact three spellings and a separately reviewed prerelease schema append are sound. Non-interrupted failures after publication need J1-R3. The restricted interrupted branch must continue omitting retentionDisclosure.
requestedDecisions.outcomeMatrix: Main governing class/code distinctions are retained, but J1-R6 adds missing native conditions; cancellation precedence is J1-R1/R2. No new public code is needed.
requestedDecisions.ephemeral: 458c read entry is the lawful producing route; E-1 to E-4 identify the owed selection, identity and trust joins. J2c remains gated on their separate reviewed dispositions and gains no write authority.
requestedDecisions.method: Separate re-commit/resume ownership and serial pre-transcribed lead sets are appropriate. Restore F2/G3 gates under J1-R5, repair S12-D under J1-R2 and clarify the SOP2 implementation edge under J1-N2. Critical-path figures remain conditional planning assumptions.
